title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
research_question: How can a pre-trained deep neural classifier be augmented with a rejection mechanism that guarantees, with high probability, a user-specified selective risk while retaining as much prediction coverage as possible?
methodology: The paper formulates selective classification in terms of risk and coverage and introduces the Selective Guaranteed Risk algorithm, which selects a confidence threshold using finite-sample probabilistic risk bounds. Two confidence-ranking mechanisms are evaluated: maximum softmax response and Monte Carlo dropout. Experiments use VGG models on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and VGG-16 and ResNet-50 on ImageNet, with held-out samples used to select thresholds and independently assess achieved risk and coverage.

key_findings.finding: The proposed procedure provides a high-probability selective-risk guarantee for a fixed classifier and confidence-ranking function, targeting Pr(R>r*) below the specified confidence parameter delta.
Softmax response and Monte Carlo dropout produced similar risk-coverage profiles on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, while softmax response was substantially better on ImageNet.
On CIFAR-10, a target risk of 1% produced test risk 0.92% with test coverage 78.56% at delta=0.001.
For ImageNet top-5 classification with ResNet-50, a target risk of 2% produced test risk 1.89% while retaining 59.35% coverage.
Across the reported risk-control experiments, the observed test risks remained below the corresponding computed bounds.

The experiments demonstrate the central selective-classification trade-off: large reductions in classification error can be obtained by abstaining on lower-confidence examples, at the cost of reduced coverage.

limitations: The method starts from a separately trained, fixed classifier rather than jointly optimizing the predictor and rejection function.
The theoretical guarantee assumes the calibration examples are sampled i.i.d. from the same underlying distribution relevant to deployment.
Achievable coverage depends on how well the selected confidence score ranks correct versus incorrect predictions.
Only standard 0/1 classification loss is studied.
The empirical study is limited to image classification on CIFAR and ImageNet and does not test distribution shift or non-image domains.
The paper identifies joint training of the classifier and selection mechanism as an important unresolved problem.
raw_claims: Selective classification allows a model to abstain rather than predict every example.
The paper represents selective performance through the relationship between risk and coverage.
The proposed algorithm chooses a confidence threshold intended to satisfy a requested risk bound with high probability.
Maximum softmax response serves as a simple confidence-ranking function.
Monte Carlo dropout is evaluated as an alternative uncertainty-based ranking mechanism.
Softmax response and Monte Carlo dropout behave similarly on the two CIFAR datasets.
Softmax response is clearly stronger than Monte Carlo dropout on the reported ImageNet experiments.
On CIFAR-10, very low selective error is attainable while retaining a substantial fraction of examples.
ImageNet experiments show that the same approach works with both VGG-16 and ResNet-50.
The paper leaves simultaneous optimization of prediction accuracy and selective coverage for future work.
